results.summary: This project implements three selectable minigames that take button input and display output on a 7-segment display. The design is written in Verilog and runs at 10 MHz. Testing is done by pressing different buttons to play the games. External hardware required includes eight buttons and a 7-segment display.

This is a Nauta operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) with 2-bit digital trimming for tuning. It is an analog design implemented at the transistor level, based on the Nauta OTA circuit with digital trim as described in referenced literature. The design is intended for analog signal processing applications. External hardware includes a power supply and measurement equipment for characterization.

Sleepy Chip is a dual-mode digital audio synthesizer featuring a 3-waveform oscillator with streaming capability and a delta-sigma DAC output. The design is controlled via SPI and includes a gate input, hardware reset, and outputs for DAC, gate LED, oscillator run, and sync. It is written in VHDL and requires a 4.8 MHz clock and an external speaker to play the music. The synthesizer supports multiple waveforms and streaming mode for continuous audio generation.

This is an 8-bit arithmetic logic unit (ALU) that performs arithmetic and bitwise operations on integer binary numbers. It uses a state machine to read two 8-bit inputs (A and B) via the 8 digital input pins, with operation control and status output over the bidirectional pins. The ALU is implemented in Verilog and is suitable for educational purposes. External hardware includes switches or buttons to provide inputs and LEDs to display results.

This is a time-domain comparator-based analog-to-digital converter (ADC). It converts analog input voltage to a digital representation using a comparator and time-domain encoding. The design is implemented in mixed-signal technology, combining analog and digital circuits. External hardware includes an analog voltage source and digital output interface for reading the conversion result.

This project is a characterization structure designed to explore fabrication process behavior. It uses standard-cell logic to implement test structures for measuring process parameters. The design is intended for silicon characterization and validation. External hardware includes measurement equipment to analyze the test structures.

This project implements a game that uses 7-segment displays and LEDs for output, with input from buttons. It includes a linear feedback shift register (LFSR) for pseudo-random number generation. The design is written in Verilog and is suitable for educational or entertainment purposes. External hardware includes buttons, 7-segment displays, and LEDs.

This project is a digital logic design that includes an ALU, register file, and logic gates. It is implemented in Verilog and demonstrates basic arithmetic and logic operations. The design is suitable for educational purposes. External hardware includes switches for input and LEDs for output.

This project is a security-focused design that includes a ROM, LFSR, and finite state machine. It outputs to a 7-segment display and is written in Verilog. The design may be used for cryptographic or security applications. External hardware includes a 7-segment display and possibly buttons for control.

This project is a lightweight design that is Tiny Tapeout friendly and has observable outputs on FPGA. It is likely a simple digital circuit or demonstration. The design is suitable for educational purposes. External hardware includes an FPGA board for implementation and testing.
